item.title: Spurs clinch rare Stamford Bridge win as Palmer sent off
item.description: Tottenham claim just their second victory over Chelsea at Stamford Bridge in 36 years, winning 2-0 as the hosts finish with 10 men after a red card for Cole Palmer.

item.title: Arsenal beat Everton to go level on points with leaders Man City
item.description: Goals from Ezri Konsa, his first for the club, and Gabriel Magalhaes helped Arsenal beat Everton 2-0 at the Emirates to move level on points with league leaders Manchester City.

item.title: Jackson scores twice as Aston Villa end Man City's perfect start
item.description: Nicolas Jackson scores twice as Aston Villa beat Manchester City 2-1 at Villa Park to end their 100% start to the Premier League season.

item.title: Bobb's late strike secures Fulham win at Coventry
item.description: Fulham's Oscar Bobb scores in the 80th minute against Coventry to earn back-to-back victories in the Premier League.

item.title: The candid meeting that 'changed' Spurs - are they finally on way back?
item.description: Tottenham end Saturday's Premier League action in 12th place, their highest league position since 2 January. Are they finally on their way back?

item.title: Man Utd not an unmanageable club - Carrick
item.description: Michael Carrick says it is possible to manage Manchester United effectively as he clings on to his job with Bournemouth visiting Old Trafford on Sunday.

item.title: From Chelsea reject to Watkins 'upgrade' - Jackson makes fast Villa start
item.description: Nicolas Jackson continues an excellent start to his Aston Villa career with a match-winning double against Manchester City.

item.title: 'A massive storage of images' - Arteta has technical area receipts
item.description: Wandering Premier League managers beware, Arsenal's Mikel Arteta has compiled a dossier of bosses leaving their technical area.

item.title: Man City's leaky defence highlights Donnarumma & Guehi struggles
item.description: Manchester City's 100% winning start to the Premier League season comes to an abrupt end against Aston Villa - leaving Enzo Maresca with glaring defensive issues to resolve.

item.title: Penders error & Palmer sees red - player ratings for Chelsea v Spurs
item.description: Goalkeeper Mike Penders endures a difficult first Premier League start, scoring an own goal in Spurs' 2-0 win at Chelsea. Here's how we - and you - rated the players.

item.title: Arsenal relieve pressure with Spurs win - can they kick on now?
item.description: Arsenal end their five-match winless run in the Women's Super League with victory at Tottenham - but can they kick on now?

item.title: Liverpool among clubs keen on Vuskovic - Sunday's gossip
item.description: Brighton defender Luka Vuskovic is being looked at by high-profile clubs, Liverpool do not intend to bring Trent Alexander-Arnold back, AC Milan are targeting Manchester United's Leny Yoro, plus more.

item.title: Hayen sacked by Burnley after just 14 games
item.description: Nicky Hayen is sacked after just 14 games in charge at Burnley following a poor start to the season.

item.title: Strikers finding form as Rangers bounce back
item.description: Derek McInnes demanded a response from his Rangers team after the disappointment of two dropped points at Dundee - and they delivered in emphatic style against St Johnstone.

item.title: Infantino says he is backed by 'vast majority'
item.description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino laughs off questions about whether he considered resigning over the World Cup sell-off debacle.

item.title: Kompany recovery will take 'weeks' as tests continue
item.description: Vincent Kompany remains stable in hospital as doctors run tests following his collapse on Friday, says Bayern Munich director Max Eberl.

item.title: Spurs boss Ho wants 'more support and training' for WSL referees
item.description: Tottenham manager Martin Ho was frustrated by a penalty decision in their defeat by Arsenal and says Women's Super League referees "need more support".

item.title: Sutton's predictions v Waffle the Wonder Dog and his owner Simon
item.description: BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton takes on Waffle the Wonder Dog and his owner Simon, plus the BBC readers and AI with his predictions for this weekend's Premier League fixtures.

item.title: Should Palmer have been sent off earlier than he was?
item.description: Match of the Day pundit Martin Keown looks at the red card shown to Cole Palmer during Chelsea's 2-0 defeat to Tottenham, with the former Arsenal defender agreeing with the decision and suggesting Palmer was lucky not to receive a straight red for an early incident.

item.title: How 'special talent' Jackson inspired Villa to victory over Man City
item.description: Match of the Day pundits Martin Keown and Steph Houghton look at the impact Aston Villa forward Nicolas Jackson had with his two goals in their 2-1 victory over Manchester City, with Keown describing him as a "special talent".

item.title: 'Best performance since I arrived' - De Zerbi praises Spurs after win
item.description: Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi describes his side's 2-0 victory over Chelsea at Stamford Bridge as "the best since he arrived at the club", adding the win was special given it was against their local rivals.

item.title: Arsenal fight back to beat Tottenham and ease pressure on Slegers
item.description: Alessia Russo scores a controversial penalty as Arsenal come from behind to beat local rivals Tottenham Hotspur 2-1 to secure just their second win of the season in the Women's Super League, and ease the pressure on manager Renee Slegers.

item.title: 'We could have played better' - Alonso disappointed after defeat
item.description: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso admitted he was disappointed by his side's performance, saying they "could have played better" following their 2-0 defeat by Tottenham at Stamford Bridge.

item.title: Huddersfield on top, but difficult days for Derby - Sam Parkin's EFL takeaways
item.description: BBC Final Score pundit Sam Parkin looks at the weekend's talking points in the EFL, including Huddersfield's fine form and QPR's big win over Swansea.

item.title: Jackson stars with two goals - player ratings for Aston Villa v Man City
item.description: How Aston Villa and Man City players rated following their Premier League match.

item.title: Barnet condemn racial abuse of Noel-Williams

item.title: Cardiff's Aberfan inspiration after emotional tribute
item.description: Cardiff City head coach Brian Barry-Murphy has spoken of the emotions surrounding tributes to the Aberfan disaster of 1966 that played a part in inspiring his side to victory over Birmingham.

item.title: Matos rues QPR display as Swansea suffer Yeo blow

item.title: 'It's harsh' - was Arsenal's winning penalty a controversial decision?
item.description: Following Arsenal's 2-1 win at rivals Tottenham Hotspur, former England footballers Ellen White, Fara Williams and Alex Scott discuss whether the away side were fortunate to be given a penalty, which proved to be the winning moment for Arsenal.

item.title: Symonds scores screamer as Brighton beat West Ham
item.description: Maisie Symonds scores a 'goal of the season' contender to help Brighton beat West Ham 3-0, securing just their second league win of the season in the Women's Super League.

item.title: Forest left frustrated as winless run goes on after draw at Ipswich
item.description: Nottingham Forest ended a run of three successive league defeats but endured another night of missed chances as they drew 1-1 at Ipswich Town in the Premier League, but the result does move the away side out of the relegation zone on goal difference.

item.title: 'It doesn't make sense' - Glasner confused after Diop avoids red card
item.description: Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner admits he was left confused by the decision to not send off Issa Diop after a VAR check during his side's 1-1 draw at Ipswich Town, but praised his side's performance and urged them to 'stay patient' as Forest's winless run stretched to four matches.

item.title: 'We had to scrap' - O'Neil praises Ipswich resilience after Forest draw
item.description: Ipswich manager Gary O'Neil praises his side's ability to "dig in and fight" as his side come from behind to earn a 1-1 draw against Nottingham Forest at Portman Road in the Premier League.

item.title: Borussia M'gladbach finally get first win after five-goal thriller
item.description: Bundesliga's bottom side Borussia Monchengladbach come from behind to beat Stuttgart 3-2, as the away side secure their first league win of the season, at the seventh attempt.
